newsitem.title: INDIA: Indians pray for victims of 1947 partition.
newsitem.headline: Indians pray for victims of 1947 partition.

text.p: People from different faiths gathered on a New Delhi riverbank on Tuesday to pray and sing in memory of the hundreds of thousands killed when the subcontinent was partitioned in 1947.
The prayers were held at Rajghat, the spot where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated on the banks of the Yamuna river after his assassination by a Hindu zealot in January 1948.
Actor and politician Sunil Dutt sat under a flowering tree and led about 50 people, most of them schoolgirls, in hymns praising Gandhi, who led India's campaign for freedom from British rule.

The sectarian violence triggered by the August 14-15 1947 creation of mainly Hindu India and Moslem-majority Pakistan caused the deaths of an estimated one million lives and the flight of at least 10 million refugees in history's largest mass migration.

Gandhi spent most of his final years trying to reconcile the subcontinent's warring religions. Religious strife has frequently flared in India. The destruction of a 16th-century Moslem mosque in a north Indian town in December 1992 triggered nationwide rioting in which over 3,000 people died.
Tuesday's prayer meeting was brought to a premature close by a monsoon shower. Afterwards, Dutt told Reuters of his memories of partition.

"I was still a small child at the time," he said. "But what I can recall vividly was the sight of a young girl getting married in a Punjab refugee camp, next to a dead body. It was a sight that changed my life."
Dutt said the victims of partition "should be recognised because they could not enjoy the fruits of freedom we have enjoyed since."
